The Children's Peace Monument, located in Hiroshima, Japan, commemorates Sadako Sasaki and the thousands of child victims of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima. Sadako Sasaki, a young girl, died of leukemia from radiation of the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima on August 6, 1945.

The development of nuclear weapons began with scientific breakthroughs in the 1930s, and the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada collaborated on the Manhattan Project during World War II. The project led to the creation of atomic bombs, which were first used in combat in August 1945 when two fission bombs were dropped on Japan. The Soviet Union later developed its own atomic bomb project.

Several individuals played significant roles in the development and deployment of atomic bombs. Jacob Beser was a lieutenant in the United States Army Air Forces who served as a radar specialist on the "Enola Gay" when it dropped the Little Boy atomic bomb on Hiroshima on August 6, 1945. He was also a crew member on the "Bockscar" when the Fat Man bomb was dropped on Nagasaki three days later. William Sterling Parsons, an American naval officer, worked as an ordnance expert on the Manhattan Project and was the weaponeer on the "Enola Gay". Morris R. Jeppson served as assistant weaponeer on the "Enola Gay", while Frederick Ashworth was the weaponeer on the "Bockscar" that dropped the Fat Man atomic bomb on Nagasaki.

The atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki had significant effects on the cities and their occupants. The Little Boy bomb, which was dropped on Hiroshima, exploded with an energy of approximately 15 kton TNT and caused widespread destruction. The Fat Man bomb, dropped on Nagasaki, was the second nuclear weapon used in warfare and marked the third-ever man-made nuclear explosion in history.

The development of nuclear weapons and the events surrounding their use have been documented in various books and projects. John Hersey's book "Hiroshima" tells the stories of six survivors of the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima, while the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" project was an early nuclear and space project of the People's Republic of China. The project involved the development of atomic and hydrogen bombs, as well as the launch of artificial satellites.
